problem: Transformer-based VLN agents (e.g. DUET) do not explicitly exploit guiding semantics (direction/landmark words, objects) in both language and vision. Their graph memory also averages panorama views uniformly and never passes the network's reasoning state from one step to the next.
motivation: Key navigation cues sit in specific instruction phrases and in specific objects/views, yet models must learn them implicitly from data. Averaging past observations loses information and breaks the continuity of reasoning across steps, which hurts long-horizon decisions.
key_idea: Add explicit semantic enhancement to both modalities (IGL for language, ASV for vision) and build a memory with adaptive panorama aggregation (GAA) plus a recurrent [MEM] token carrying reasoning states between steps (RMF), on top of the DUET dual-scale graph.
insight: Both semantic modules help alone and gain more together: SR goes from 69.18 to 72.50 on R2R val-unseen, with SPL from 60.28 to 61.56. Learned view weighting (GAA) beats mean pooling (SR 71.39 to 72.50). The recurrent memory needs global, local and text [CLS] inputs; removing text drops SR to 70.63, below the no-RMF row at 72.16. The best number of objects per image is 3.
method: Semantic-role parser + IGL: NLTK extracts direction and landmark phrases, with entities normalized to 43 MP3D categories. Multi-head attention from BERT context features to these phrase embeddings gives guided features, and a sigmoid gate mixes guided and context features.

ASV: Per-image object features (geometry, angle, label, navigable type; top-M by area, walls and ceilings filtered) go through a transformer across all 36xM objects. A second transformer runs over the 36 ViT image features. Object features are averaged per image and concatenated with image features, then projected to the semantic-aware visual representation.
GAA: Replaces DUET's mean pooling of panorama views with a learned tanh + softmax attention over views, so each node in the global map gets an adaptive weighted sum.

RMF: The [CLS] tokens of the global fusion, local fusion and language streams are concatenated, linearly projected and layer-normed into a memory vector. It is written into a separate [MEM] token of both the global and local sequences at the next step.

Cross-modal fusion + dynamic decision: Two LXMERT-style encoders fuse language with global and local visual tokens. DUET's dynamic gating combines global and local action scores. Training uses cross-entropy loss.
Training scheme: Pre-training (400k iterations) runs without IGL and RMF, to avoid MLM leakage and because the recurrent state cannot be used for SAP. Both are added at fine-tuning.

setting.backbone: DUET-style dual-scale graph transformer (BERT 9 layers, ViT-B/16 features, LXMERT cross-modal encoders), trained and fine-tuned
setting.training_data: R2R (21,576 instructions) and REVERIE (21,702 instructions) with pre-training, plus REVERIE object features; no extra synthetic data mentioned
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB (36 views, ViT-B/16) + object labels/boxes from REVERIE + instruction
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (global map node selection)
setting.privileged: Object annotations (labels/boxes) provided by the REVERIE dataset; otherwise none

numbers.evidence: Table 1, comparison with SOTA on R2R, Validation Unseen

numbers_note: R2R table values are printed as integers for most metrics. The ablations report R2R val-unseen with more decimals (SR 72.50, SPL 61.56, NE 3.00, OSR 80.97), which differs from the rounded main-table row.
results: DSRG beats DUET on R2R test-unseen (SR 72 vs 69, SPL 61 vs 59) and on val-unseen (SR 73 vs 72). It also beats DUET on REVERIE test-unseen (SR 54.04 vs 52.51, SPL 37.09 vs 36.06). On R2R val-unseen SPL, TD-STP (63) is higher than DSRG (62). Gains on REVERIE are larger on the seen split.
limitations: Gains over DUET are modest on unseen splits (about 1-3 points), and there are no significance tests or multiple seeds.
Depends on REVERIE-provided object annotations and rule-based NLTK parsing of directions and landmarks; the parsing is not adapted to other languages or datasets.
IGL and RMF cannot be used in pre-training, so they are only trained during fine-tuning.
